"Didi, it's one a.m. Why is your light on?" Yogesh yawned, rubbing his eyes in the doorway.
"The coin problem. I've rewritten this recurrence four times and every version is wrong."
"So?"
"So I'm staying until it works."
"Last week you slept on that sorting bug and fixed it at breakfast."
"That was a bug. This is different." Mahima pressed her palms on her eyes. "My head is just noise. Fine. I'll write down exactly where I'm stuck and go to bed."
The next morning she burst into the kitchen. "Yogesh! It depends on the smaller amounts, one step back each time. I can see it now!"
"I haven't had chai yet."
"You were right. I slept and the pieces sorted themselves."

What is Mahima feeling about the problem at one a.m.?

qa.q: What other approach could Mahima try when stuck, and why?
qa.a: She could explain the problem aloud or work a tiny case by hand, because saying it in pieces can expose the missing step faster than staring at it.

qa.a: Yogesh sees a tired sister stuck on one problem, and reminds her that sleeping fixed a bug last week, which nudges her to stop.

subtype: Approach: sleeping on an unclear question [Thinking]
passage: It was 1:40 am in the hostel, the night before our coding test, and I'd been staring at the same dynamic programming problem for an hour. I'm Gurpreet. The problem asked for the number of ways to climb stairs with some steps broken. I had three pages of scribbles and nothing clicked. Suraj, my roommate, mumbled from his bed, "Just sleep, yaar. Your brain's soup." I wanted to keep fighting it. But I noticed I was rereading the same line without seeing it. So I wrote the problem on a sticky note, stuck it on my water bottle, and slept. At 7, brushing my teeth, it simply appeared: the ways to reach a step are the ways to reach the step before plus the one before that, and a broken step has zero ways. I laughed with toothpaste in my mouth. Looking back, the night's sleep did what the hour of staring couldn't.

qa.q: What time was it when Gurpreet was stuck?
How was Gurpreet feeling at 1:40 am?
qa.a: Gurpreet felt frustrated and stubborn, wanting to keep fighting the problem even while rereading the same line.

qa.q: What else could Gurpreet try when stuck late at night?
qa.a: Gurpreet could set a stop time, write down what is known so far, and trust that a rested mind will see it more clearly.

qa.q: How does Suraj see Gurpreet's late-night struggle?
qa.a: Suraj sees a tired mind going in circles and bluntly suggests sleep, which turns out to be good advice.

grounding: Shows a student stuck late at night on a dynamic programming problem stopping, sleeping, and seeing the recurrence clearly in the morning.

passage:
Warden's diary, girls' hostel, Thursday.
Past midnight on my round I found Vinita still at the common-room table, placement practice book open, head in her hands. Her roommate Hafsa had already gone up. Vinita said she'd been stuck for over an hour on one dynamic programming problem, something about cutting a rod, and couldn't bear to leave it unsolved before Saturday's test. I asked her to write down exactly where she was stuck, then go to bed. She argued a little, then did it.
At breakfast she came to find me, eyes bright. She said that in the morning, before she had even brushed her teeth, she saw that each length's best price depends only on the best prices of the smaller lengths. It had simply arrived. Hafsa teased her for smiling at her idli.
Next time I see a light on past midnight before a test, I'll send them to sleep sooner.

qa.q: How was Vinita feeling past midnight?
qa.a: Vinita was frustrated and anxious, head in her hands, unable to bear leaving the problem unsolved before Saturday.

qa.q: What else could Vinita do before sleeping on a problem?
qa.a: Vinita could write the stuck point on a card, as she did, and set a firm stop time so it doesn't run past midnight.

qa.q: How does the warden see the result?
qa.a: The warden sees that sleep helped Vinita solve it and resolves to send students to bed sooner next time.

grounding: Illustrates a student stuck late on a dynamic programming problem who, told to stop and sleep, sees the recurrence clearly the next morning.
